content: RFC 7009 mandates invalid/already-revoked tokens return success (no error) so revocation-endpoint success does not prove the token was ever valid or actually revoked -- cannot distinguish 'revoked' from 'provider silently no-op'd' from client side. unsupported_token_type error exists but many providers ignore token_type_hint. Must design explicit per-credential revocation result states (revoked / discarded_revocation_unsupported / failed) rather than trusting HTTP 200.
